mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC (from -45.6% to -36.7%) indicates recovery momentum in consumer mobility. This trend continues linearly over the next four weeks, producing net positive direction in RETAIL_REC relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 8.9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC four-week mean falls below -36.7% or declines week-on-week in three of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility recovery (from -43.4% to -33.0%, a 10.4 point improvement) enables commuter access to retail districts. When TRANSIT rises above -30%, retail footfall increases within one week as workers resume in-person schedules and shopping patterns.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -33.0% in t-0w, closest to threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week of TRANSIT crossing -30%, or TRANSIT remains below -35% for all four forecast weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of WORKPLACES recovery (from -49.0% to -44.3%) and PARKS normalization (from -14.9% to +0.7%) signals confidence in public mobility. This dual signal triggers discretionary retail visits within two weeks as behavioral risk aversion declines.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves >3 points AND PARKS reaches positive territory
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS crossed zero in t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in weeks t+1 or t+2, or PARKS returns to negative values while WORKPLACES stalls below -45%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM decline (from -21.7% to -11.3%) indicates easing of essential-only mobility restrictions. When essential-category mobility normalizes, policy constraints on discretionary retail relax, enabling RETAIL_REC recovery within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 10.4 points over four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM reverses by >3 points in any single week, or RETAIL_REC four-week mean remains below -40%.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September timing (t-0w = 2021-09-15) coincides with back-to-school and autumn retail seasonality in Lombardy. Seasonal demand lift compounds with observed mobility recovery, producing accelerating RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC four-week mean is lower than the preceding four-week mean, or week-on-week growth rate decelerates in three of four forecast weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility decline (from 11.0% to 8.7%) indicates residents spending less time at home, consistent with increased out-of-home activity. This outbound shift sustains retail visits over the next two weeks as mobility patterns normalize.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 9% in any week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 10% in either of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines week-on-week in both weeks t+1 and t+2.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement across TRANSIT (-33.0%), WORKPLACES (-44.3%), and RETAIL_REC (-36.7%) reflects coordinated return to pre-pandemic mobility patterns. This multi-domain synchronization indicates sustained behavioral shift, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks as confidence solidifies.
candidate_trigger: all three proxies improve >5 points from t-3w to t-0w
evidence_refs: fact:All three improved over four-week window
failure_condition: Any of the three proxies reverses by >8 points in a single week, or RETAIL_REC four-week mean falls below -38%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS normalization (from -14.9% to +0.7%) signals public confidence in outdoor gathering. When parks reach positive mobility, retail districts within or adjacent to parks experience spillover foot traffic within one week, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS reaches or exceeds 0% in any week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in week t+1 following PARKS crossing 0%, or PARKS returns to negative territory in the forecast period.
